title: How would you estimate how many home EV chargers are installed in the UK each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many home EV chargers are installed in the UK each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A chain of shares: new electric cars, then buyers with a driveway, then those who install a charger. Then a reality check against 2025 sales. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many home EV chargers are installed in the UK each year?

The approach

New electric cars × share bought by people with a driveway × share who install a charger.

Tip: When you finish, say what the number means for the client, not just the number.

Step by step

  1. New fully electric cars sold in the UK per year: 400k
  2. × 60% buyers with off-street parking
  3. × 80% of those who install a home charger

That gives about 192k chargers a year.

Does it make sense?

Second-hand electric car buyers add more installs each year.

Real-world check

About 473,000 new battery electric cars were registered in the UK in 2025 (SMMT), more than the 400,000 assumed here. Rerun with that figure and you get about 230,000 home chargers, a good reminder to update an input when you learn a better one.

Source: SMMT: new car registrations, December 2025.

New-car buyers are only part of installation demand

The initial estimate is 192,000 home chargers associated with new fully electric cars, based on 400,000 car sales, 60% off-street parking access and 80% installation uptake. It misses some used-car buyers who install a charger for the first time and some households replacing an existing unit.

Suppose, separately, 150,000 used EV purchasers are first-time EV households, half have suitable parking and 70% install. That adds about 52,500 chargers. Combined with the illustrative new-car estimate, total would be around 245,000 before replacement demand. These are practice inputs, not verified UK volumes.

Beware of assuming one charger per car. A two-EV household may share a single unit. If the client's business is installing chargers rather than manufacturing them, the price and market size should include electrician labour, site work and any hardware sold through partners, without counting the same value twice.
